name: Donald Trump
why: Presidential statements can change exchange-rate, trade, Fed and crypto expectations. Economic exposure must remain analytically separate from motive claims.

name: Scott Bessent
why: Treasury directs U.S. FX intervention and debt management. Bessent has a long global-macro/currency background, making changes in Treasury signaling especially important.

name: Kevin Warsh
why: Monetary policy can reinforce dollar-devaluation pressure or create the opposite dollar-squeeze regime.

name: Stephen Miran
role: Federal Reserve Governor / former CEA chair
why: His published work discusses structural dollar overvaluation and mechanisms for changing international monetary arrangements.

name: Treasury debt-management / ESF officials
why: Operational implementation can reveal policy intent before high-level rhetoric becomes explicit.

name: USTR / Commerce
why: Trade policy can create incentives for currency realignment and can provoke foreign retaliation or capital-flow changes.

name: OMB / NEC / CEA
why: Budget and economic-policy choices determine whether a weaker-dollar strategy becomes a fiscal-dominance problem.

name: Federal Reserve Board / FOMC
why: The Fed is the main counterforce or amplifier for both debasement and dollar-funding-squeeze regimes.

name: China PBOC / SAFE
why: China can reduce structural dollar dependence gradually without needing or wanting a disorderly dollar crash.

name: Japan MOF / BOJ
role: Large Treasury holder / FX intervention actor
why: Japan is a major marginal buyer of Treasuries and a key participant in coordinated currency policy.

name: ECB / SNB / European reserve managers
why: The dollar is valued relative to alternatives; weakness or strength in Europe can offset U.S.-specific risk.

name: BRICS / India / Brazil / Russia / Gulf states
why: External actors can reduce structural dollar demand even without coordinating a sudden attack.

name: Global macro funds / CTAs / asset managers
why: Private capital can turn policy vulnerability into a rapid market move long before reserve managers change reported holdings.

name: Stablecoin issuers / custodians
why: Stablecoins can strengthen transactional dollar usage while adding issuer, reserve and redemption channels that need separate monitoring.
